subject: Mediva Hosting: residency, egress window & limited ops access request
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@medivahealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medivahealth.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency & egress controls for Private pilot

Hi Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal ran a quick review and surfaced two must-haves for the pilot:

1) Data residency: all customer data (inference payloads, logs, and backups) must remain inside our VPC region and not be exported to Redwood-managed systems for at least 12 months.
2) Audit access: Mediva will require the ability to request an on-site or remote audit with 14 days' notice, but we want to restrict access to a scoped set of telemetry (no raw PII payloads), and we prefer that any log extraction is controlled by Mediva and delivered under our export process.

We understand this is non-standard. In exchange, Mediva is requesting a 25% pilot discount and a 60-day implementation credit to cover validation work. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept timeboxed residency + a constrained audit process for a pilot?

Attachments: Mediva_legal_redlines_06072026.pdf (redline summary)

Best,
Anya
Procurement 
Mediva Health

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & egress controls for Private pilot

Jordan — forwarding Mediva's ask. Karthik / Lauren, can Deal Desk / Legal advise on tolerance and exec path here?

Quick thoughts:
- Residency-only (no outbound egress) for 12 months is a hard constraint operationally; we can offer a timeboxed carveout but need engineering to sign off on support model and monitoring.
- Audit access needs precise language; if we limit extractions to aggregated telemetry and require Mediva to sign an NDA + SOP, that may be acceptable.
- Commercial ask (25% + 60d credit) is material; recommend escalation to Laura for leadership exception.

I pulled rough impact numbers: estimated incremental engineering ops ~$45k for the pilot setup and ongoing runbook maintenance ~$6k/mo. If leadership is open, suggest a counter: 18% pilot discount, one-time $40k implementation credit, 9-month residency embargo (not 12).

Attaching: Redwood_Proposed_SLA_Redline_20260608.docx (draft counter-redline).

- Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & egress controls for Private pilot

Team — legal/security input below. High level: we can accept a timeboxed residency/egress embargo for a pilot provided:

- Residency window is explicit (start/end dates) and terminates automatically, no perpetual carveout.
- Audit scope language must enumerate allowed telemetry categories and explicitly exclude raw inference payloads containing PII.
- Any log extraction requires a signed export request and must be performed under Redwood supervision; copies are delivered to Mediva, rollback possible.
- KMS key ownership: prefer Mediva-managed keys in the VPC (Bring-your-own-KMS) for any at-rest encryption; if not possible, use a split-key escrow model.

Commercial: legal will not block up to 20% discount for a named pilot if product/ops risk is mitigated. I recommend we request a 1) formal security questionnaire completion, 2) SOC2 in-scope confirmation, and 3) a written SLA appendix that defines audit boundaries.

Proposed immediate response to Mediva: offer a 20% pilot discount, $35k implementation credit, 9-month residency embargo with explicit end date, KMS-by-customer requirement or split-key fallback, and a restricted audit process (14-day notice, scoped telemetry).

Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Residency & egress controls for Private pilot — leadership clearance request

Laura — forwarding the thread. Short summary: Mediva requests a 12-month no-egress residency and broad audit access; Marissa/Karthik propose we offer a constrained pilot concession (9 months), KMS-by-customer, scoped audit, and a blended commercial counter. Legal is comfortable up to 20% discount if controls are in place.

Why this needs leadership: the concession sets a precedent for residency carveouts and has quantifiable ops uplift. Impact estimate: ~$45k initial engineering + ongoing runbook support; revenue impact if we accept 20% discount for the first 12 months of committed usage ~ $120k.

Ask: do you approve escalating this exception with the following guardrails?
1) Approve 9-month residency embargo (timeboxed).
2) Approve up to 20% pilot discount + $35k implementation credit.
3) Require customer-managed KMS or split-key escrow.
4) Approve scoped audit language only (no raw PII payload extraction).

If yes, we'll draft a conditional addendum for signature and move to DocuSign.

— Jordan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Residency & egress controls for Private pilot — leadership clearance request

Thanks for the concise summary. I approve an exception on the following conditional terms (leadership clearance granted):

1) Residency window: 9 months max. Add automatic sunset clause that returns to standard SLA after the window.
2) Commercial: approve up to 18% pilot discount (not 20%) and a $35k one-time implementation credit. Finance to confirm final pricing impact and sign-off.
3) Security controls: customer-managed KMS required where possible; if not, escrow split-key with attestations.
4) Audit: strictly scoped telemetry only; any extraction requires a signed export request + security review; require a pre-authorized SOP and 14-day notice.
5) Operational readiness: engineering runbook and an internal on-call rotation for pilot support; Ops to estimate staffing cadence and confirm feasibility before legal signs the addendum.

Action owners: Marissa — finalize the commercial terms; Karthik — finalize redline with the audit/KMS language; Jordan — prepare addendum and shared DocuSign link; Laura (me) — will approve the final doc after finance and ops confirm cost/operational impact.

Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
